issues.reason: "Keepers" (bare plural) and "wintergloss" (bare mass) are bare kind-denoting NPs on both sides, which is the stated mechanical trigger for the opaque kind-level relation, so the per-instance Implication wrongly distributes to every keeper a predication the instruction set says must stay opaque ("does this mosquito carry malaria?" correctly stays unknown) — the prompt's own "Foxes rarely cross the causeway" rule-example has a DEFINITE object, which is exactly why it is not a kind relation.

Compound concepts' default for a transparently modifier+head solid spelling is "always emit the genus … the solid spelling is never a reason to skip decomposition"; suppression requires an established IS-A failure (the hot-dog test), which a coined fiction noun does not supply — the reviewer's own gap concedes the test has no determinate answer here.

gaps_confirmed: deciding whether a coined / invented solid-spelling common noun ("wintergloss") is transparently modifier + head: the only stated test is the IS-A / hot-dog check, which is indeterminate for fiction vocabulary the reader has no world knowledge of
defect_summary: The compliant form is the opaque kind-level relation (Burn keeper wintergloss) at strength 0.1 / confidence 0.9 (the "rarely" dial applied to the relation atom itself), keeping the existing (QuantifierPhrase keeper burn "rarely") companion on the subject kind, and emitting no per-instance Implication.
notes: The frequency dial value, the companion's shape and TV, and the compound genus are all fine; only the construction routing fails. Nothing false is asserted by the rule per se — the defect is that it distributes an opaque kind characterization to every instance.
